analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation edit to docs/threat-model.yaml. At base line 1969 and head lines 1969-1970, the T-050 media-ingestion mitigation text now says that accepted inline video MIME types are data:video/mp4, data:video/x-m4v, data:video/quicktime and data:video/mov, and that the bytes must be an MP4 or QuickTime file. The existing decoded-byte, duration, frame-pixel, video-count and aggregate caps are unchanged. The text also still says http(s), file and unsupported container types are rejected. The supplied units cover only base lines 1-897, which contain header comments, the adversaries, assets, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011 and T-007 to T-010. The changed hunk near line 1969 is outside the supplied text, so I could not check the T-050 surrounding context or any provider source. No supplied evidence shows a security control weakened or a threat assumption invalidated. The edit is documentation only and changes no code, endpoint or deployment. One unverified contract remains: the provider media-ingestion code (the Swift video decoding path under provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference or similar) is not in this batch. It would need to implement the added MIME aliases (x-m4v, mov) and the byte-signature check for the doc to be accurate. The doc newly claims content-sniffing of MP4/QuickTime bytes, which the code diff, if any, should confirm. Related threats are T-050 (TB-003, temporary-file exposure of inline video plaintext) and the container reference restriction. A later pass should verify the code matches the doc, including that the file-based temporary-file handling is still the mitigated path. No regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
